name: CI/CD Pipelines
scope: A person with INTERMEDIATE proficiency level in CI/CD Pipelines as a competency should be able to design, configure, and optimize end-to-end CI/CD pipelines using major platforms like Jenkins, GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, CircleCI, and cloud-native tools; model workflows covering build, test (unit, integration, E2E), packaging, deployment, and release stages for multi-environment (dev, QA, staging, prod) scenarios; integrate build tools (Maven, Gradle, npm, pip, .NET), manage dependencies, artifact versioning, and publishing to registries (e.g., Artifactory, Nexus, Docker Hub, ECR); implement parallelization, caching, conditional logic, reusable templates, and shared libraries/orbs; configure automated and gated deployments to VMs, containers, Kubernetes (manifests, Helm), and handle rollback, feature flags, and database migrations; integrate Infrastructure-as-Code (Terraform, CloudFormation, ARM, Kubernetes YAML), manage ephemeral environments, and sequence infra/app changes; embed security scans (SAST, DAST, dependency/image scanning), enforce secrets management using CI/CD secret stores or external managers, and apply compliance gates (audit logging, approvals); monitor pipeline health and metrics (duration, failure rate, MTTR), set up notifications, analyze bottlenecks, and optimize for speed, cost, and reliability; troubleshoot and debug failures (logs, artifacts, reruns, local reproduction), handle flaky tests, and collaborate on cross-cutting issues; maintain documentation, SOPs, runbooks, and knowledge sharing for pipeline usage and troubleshooting; and participate in governance, code reviews, and process integration with development, QA, security, and operations teams, aligning pipelines with branching, release, and change management strategies.

{"sections":[{"name":"Core CI/CD Concepts & Principles","scope_included":"- Understand and articulate the full CI/CD lifecycle (code → build → test → package → deploy → verify → release) and where each pipeline stage fits
- Distinguish clearly between Continuous Integration, Continuous Delivery, and Continuous Deployment, and identify which model a given team is practicing
- Apply core CI principles: frequent integration, fast feedback, automated verification, trunk-based or well-structured branching, and keeping main branch always releasable
- Apply core CD principles: automated, repeatable deployments; environment parity; small, incremental releases; and quick rollback capability
- Model pipelines as code-centric workflows driven by version control events (push, PR/MR, tag, schedule) rather than manual triggers
- Reason about pipeline performance (time-to-feedback), reliability (flake rate, failure modes), and maintainability as first-class concerns
- Understand the role of CI/CD in broader SDLC practices such as DevOps, GitOps, and trunk-based development, and how it enforces quality gates
- Recognize common anti-patterns (long-lived feature branches, manual promotion steps, monolithic jobs, tight coupling to specific environments) and know how to mitigate them at an intermediate level","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Pipeline Design & Workflow Modeling","scope_included":"- Design end-to-end pipelines for small to medium-sized applications or services, covering build, test, package, and deploy stages
- Decompose pipelines into appropriate stages/jobs (e.g., checkout, build, unit test, integration test, security scan, package, deploy, smoke test) with clear dependencies
- Implement parallelization within pipelines (e.g., parallel test suites, parallel builds for multiple services or platforms) to reduce overall runtime
- Design branching-based workflows (e.g., main/develop/release branches; feature branches) and map them to pipeline behaviors (e.g., what runs on PR vs on main vs on tags)
- Configure pipelines for different event triggers: pushes, pull/merge requests, scheduled runs (nightly builds), manual approvals, and tag-based releases
- Define and implement promotion flows across environments (e.g., dev → QA → staging → production) using automated gates and controlled approvals where needed
- Implement fan-in/fan-out patterns (e.g., multi-repo or monorepo scenarios) where multiple components must be built/tested before a combined deploy
- Introduce basic pipeline reusability (e.g., shared templates, re-usable workflows, shared libraries, or orbs/extensions depending on the platform)
- Apply basic optimization patterns: caching of dependencies, selective test execution, incremental builds, and conditional stages based on changed paths or tags
- Ensure pipelines are idempotent and stateless where possible, relying on artifacts and configuration rather than mutable shared environments","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Build & Dependency Management in Pipelines","scope_included":"- Configure CI pipelines to perform reproducible builds using language-specific build tools (e.g., Maven/Gradle for Java, npm/yarn for Node.js, pip/poetry for Python, .NET build tools)
- Manage dependency installation and caching within pipelines to balance speed and reproducibility
- Implement build versioning strategies (e.g., semantic versioning, build numbers, git-based versioning) and embed version metadata into artifacts
- Configure artifact packaging steps (e.g., JAR/WAR, NuGet packages, npm packages, container images, OS packages) as part of the pipeline
- Integrate with artifact repositories/registries (e.g., artifact registries for binaries and container registries for images) for publishing and consuming build artifacts
- Implement deterministic container image builds using Dockerfiles or equivalent, including multi-stage builds to optimize image size and security posture
- Ensure that build outputs are immutable, traceable to source commits, and promoted across environments without rebuilding
- Handle multi-module or multi-service builds (e.g., monorepo setups) with correct dependency graphs and partial builds when only some modules change
- Understand and implement basic supply chain integrity measures in the build process (e.g., checksums, provenance metadata, signing of artifacts or images where supported)
- Diagnose and fix common build failures related to dependency resolution, version conflicts, environmental differences, and tooling updates","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Automated Testing Integration within Pipelines","scope_included":"- Integrate multiple layers of automated tests into the pipeline: unit tests, component/integration tests, and basic end-to-end or smoke tests
- Configure pipelines to fail fast on critical test failures and to block merges/releases when tests do not pass
- Use test reports (e.g., JUnit/XML formats, coverage reports) within CI systems to surface pass/fail status, flakiness, and historical trends
- Implement test coverage measurement and enforce minimum coverage thresholds where appropriate
- Configure selective test execution based on changes (e.g., run only relevant test suites for modified components when feasible)
- Integrate static analysis and code quality tools (e.g., linters, code formatters, code quality analyzers) as part of the CI pipeline
- Integrate dynamic tests such as basic API or UI smoke tests in post-deployment stages to validate deployments in target environments
- Handle flaky tests by identifying them, quarantining or tagging, and setting up separate jobs where needed to avoid blocking critical flows
- Use containerized or ephemeral test environments (e.g., using docker-compose or test containers) within CI for integration tests
- Ensure that test data and environment configuration are handled predictably (e.g., seeded databases, fixtures, mock services) to make tests reliable in CI","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Deployment Strategies & Release Management","scope_included":"- Implement automated deployments from pipelines to non-production environments (dev, QA, staging) and semi-automated/controlled deployments to production
- Configure deployment jobs for common platforms: application servers, VMs, containers, and Kubernetes clusters via deployment manifests or Helm charts
- Apply basic deployment strategies such as rolling updates, blue-green, and canary deployments with pipeline-driven orchestration where supported
- Set up pre-deployment and post-deployment checks (e.g., health checks, smoke tests, basic monitoring checks) within the pipeline
- Implement safe rollback mechanisms, including pipeline steps to roll back to previously known-good versions or configurations
- Manage environment-specific configuration (e.g., environment variables, configuration files, parameterization) within the pipeline in a controlled manner
- Use feature flags/toggles in coordination with pipelines to decouple deployments from feature releases where organizational practices allow
- Coordinate tagged releases and release branches with pipeline behavior (e.g., tags triggering production builds and deployments)
- Integrate database change deployment strategies (e.g., migration scripts, schema migration tools) into pipelines with basic rollback/roll-forward considerations
- Understand limitations and risks of fully automated production deployment vs. gated/manual approval flows, and configure appropriate controls accordingly","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Infrastructure-as-Code & Environment Management in Pipelines","scope_included":"- Integrate Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) workflows (e.g., Terraform, CloudFormation, ARM/Bicep, Kubernetes manifests/Helm) as stages in CI/CD pipelines
- Implement automated validation of IaC (linting, formatting, static analysis, plan generation) before applying changes
- Configure pipelines to apply IaC changes to cloud or on-prem environments in a controlled, reviewable manner (e.g., plan → approval → apply pattern)
- Use environment-specific variables, parameter files, or workspaces to manage multiple environments (dev, test, staging, prod) from shared IaC definitions
- Manage lifecycle of ephemeral environments (e.g., per-branch or per-PR environments) for testing and tear them down via pipeline automation
- Understand and manage dependencies between application deployments and infrastructure changes within pipelines (e.g., sequencing infra updates before app deploy)
- Implement basic drift detection and reconciliation workflows triggered via pipelines (e.g., regular IaC plan checks or GitOps-style reconciliation)
- Coordinate Kubernetes-related CI/CD flows, including applying manifests, Helm releases, and basic GitOps-style deployments using appropriate tools
- Handle secure storage and retrieval of IaC backend credentials (e.g., Terraform state backends, cloud provider credentials) via pipeline-integrated secret stores
- Diagnose and resolve common IaC pipeline issues, such as locking problems, failed plans/applies, and inconsistent state across environments","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Security, Compliance & Secrets Management in Pipelines","scope_included":"- Integrate security scanning steps into pipelines: dependency vulnerability scans, container image scans, and basic static application security testing
- Configure pipelines to enforce security gates (e.g., breaking builds on high-severity vulnerabilities or license policy violations) with appropriate thresholds
- Manage credentials and secrets (API keys, passwords, certificates, tokens) using built-in CI secret stores or external secret managers, avoiding plaintext in code or logs
- Apply least-privilege principles to CI/CD service accounts, agents, and deployment credentials, and understand the impact of misconfigured permissions
- Ensure secure handling of environment variables and configuration files, including masking secrets in logs and isolating secure variables per environment
- Understand and apply basic compliance-related practices in pipelines (e.g., audit logging of deployments, approvals for production changes, separation of duties where required)
- Integrate code signing, artifact signing, or image signing into the pipeline where organizational practices require it
- Configure pipelines to run security tools in both CI (pre-merge) and CD (pre-deploy) stages to catch issues early and before production deployment
- Recognize common CI/CD-specific security risks (e.g., exposed tokens, untrusted third-party actions/plugins, running unvalidated code in privileged runners) and mitigate them at an intermediate level
- Participate in handling security incident responses related to CI/CD (e.g., revoking compromised tokens, rotating secrets, invalidating vulnerable artifacts, tightening pipeline policies)","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Observability, Feedback & Pipeline Optimization","scope_included":"- Use CI/CD platform dashboards and logs to monitor pipeline health (success/failure trends, duration per stage/job, queue times, flaky stages)
- Set and track basic KPIs for pipelines such as build duration, deployment frequency, change failure rate, and mean time to recovery for failed pipeline runs
- Configure notifications and alerts (e.g., chat, email, issue trackers) for critical pipeline events, such as failed builds on main, failed production deployments, or degraded performance
- Analyze pipeline bottlenecks (e.g., long-running tests, slow build steps, contention on shared runners) and implement optimization measures
- Implement caching strategies for dependencies and build artifacts to reduce execution time while maintaining correctness
- Use pipeline artifacts and logs effectively for debugging failures and for historical troubleshooting
- Introduce and manage basic pipeline resiliency practices, such as retry logic for transient failures, explicit timeouts, and robust cleanup steps
- Implement branch and path-based filtering to avoid running unnecessary jobs on irrelevant changes where supported
- Understand the cost implications of pipeline executions (e.g., compute usage, SaaS billing) and optimize pipeline design to balance speed, reliability, and cost
- Participate in continuous improvement of CI/CD practices by analyzing incidents, post-mortems, and metrics to propose and implement concrete pipeline enhancements","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Troubleshooting, Debugging & Failure Handling in Pipelines","scope_included":"- Systematically debug failed pipeline runs by examining logs, artifacts, exit codes, and recent changes in code or configuration
- Differentiate between infrastructure, configuration, test, and application-related failures and narrow down root causes effectively at an intermediate level
- Reproduce pipeline issues locally or in isolated environments (e.g., using containerized runners) when needed for deeper diagnosis
- Use CI/CD platform features such as rerun/reattempt, run with SSH/debug mode, or job-level retries appropriately and safely
- Diagnose and fix common pipeline misconfigurations: wrong paths, mis-ordered dependencies, missing environment variables, incorrect secrets, or incompatible tool versions
- Handle intermittent/external failures gracefully by adding retries, backoff, and clearer error handling where applicable
- Implement clear error and logging strategies within pipeline scripts and jobs to make future troubleshooting easier
- Analyze historical pipeline failures to identify patterns (e.g., certain jobs are often flaky, failures after specific dependency updates) and implement mitigations
- Collaborate with other teams (infrastructure, security, application dev) to resolve cross-cutting CI/CD issues that span code, infra, and tooling
- Document resolved issues and their fixes in a structured way so that recurring problems are handled more quickly in the future","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Tooling Ecosystem & Platform Usage","scope_included":"- Operate confidently one or more major CI/CD platforms (e.g., Jenkins, GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, CircleCI, Bitbucket Pipelines, Bamboo, cloud-native CI/CD services) at an intermediate user level
- Author, read, and maintain pipeline configurations in the platform’s configuration language (e.g., YAML, Groovy, domain-specific DSLs) with attention to readability and maintainability
- Configure and manage build agents/runners (self-hosted or shared), including selecting appropriate executors (docker, shell, VM) and understanding their constraints
- Integrate the CI/CD platform with version control systems, issue trackers, artifact registries, notification tools, and chat/communication tools
- Use marketplace/community plugins, extensions, or shared actions/runners responsibly, understanding their capabilities, security implications, and versioning
- Configure pipeline concurrency and resource controls (e.g., parallelism, job limits, queues, labels) to improve throughput and isolation
- Set up basic access controls and permissions within the CI/CD platform (e.g., who can trigger deployments, who can modify pipeline configurations)
- Perform routine maintenance tasks in the CI/CD platform (upgrading agents, rotating tokens, cleaning up old artifacts/workspaces) as per team procedures
- Evaluate when to introduce new CI/CD tools or platform features (e.g., dynamic environments, templates, reusable workflows, pipelines as code in separate repos) and participate in their adoption
- Understand high-level differences between traditional CI servers, SaaS CI/CD platforms, and GitOps-focused tools, and choose appropriate approaches for given use cases","is_non_core_section":true},{"name":"Configuration, Templates & Reuse of Pipeline Logic","scope_included":"- Structure pipeline configuration files for clarity, reuse, and modularity (e.g., splitting long configurations into reusable templates or includes)
- Define and use pipeline variables/parameters, matrices, and reusable snippets to avoid duplication and support configuration per branch or environment
- Implement shared libraries, orbs, templates, or composite actions (depending on platform) to centralize common steps (e.g., standard build/test/deploy patterns)
- Maintain shared pipeline components in version control with proper versioning, changelogs, and backward compatibility considerations
- Configure conditional logic in pipelines (e.g., run jobs only on specific branches, tags, or when files in certain paths change)
- Use configuration inheritance, anchors, or equivalent mechanisms to enforce organizational standards across multiple repositories
- Separate environment-specific configuration from pipeline logic while still enabling easy overrides and secure storage of sensitive values
- Implement simple plugin or action wrappers to enforce standards (e.g., standardized static analysis step, common security scan step)
- Review and refactor existing pipeline configurations to reduce complexity, remove dead code, and align with updated best practices
- Participate in defining and propagating organization-wide CI/CD templates and patterns for new services and repositories","is_non_core_section":true},{"name":"Collaboration, Governance & Process Integration","scope_included":"- Collaborate with developers, QA, operations, and security teams to translate workflow requirements into practical, automated CI/CD pipelines
- Participate in code reviews of pipeline and deployment configurations, providing and receiving feedback on structure, safety, and maintainability
- Align pipeline behaviors with team branching, release, and environment strategies (e.g., release trains, trunk-based development, GitFlow adaptations)
- Incorporate change management processes into pipelines where required (e.g., approvals, change tickets, change windows) without over-manualizing workflows
- Help define and enforce team-level policies via CI/CD (e.g., mandatory checks before merge, required reviews, required quality or security gates)
- Communicate clearly about the impact of pipeline changes on teams (e.g., new checks, new deployment behaviors, changes to triggers) and coordinate rollout
- Provide onboarding support to new team members on how to interact with pipelines, interpret results, and troubleshoot basic issues themselves
- Work with product and delivery leads to ensure CI/CD practices support desired release cadences and reliability goals
- Gather feedback from stakeholders on pipeline pain points (e.g., long build times, unclear failures, slow releases) and prioritize improvement tasks
- Participate in broader DevOps and platform-engineering initiatives, representing CI/CD considerations in architecture and design discussions","is_non_core_section":true},{"name":"Documentation & Knowledge Sharing for Pipelines","scope_included":"- Maintain clear, up-to-date documentation for pipelines, including build/test/deploy stages, triggers, required environment variables, and secrets usage
- Document standard operating procedures (SOPs) for common CI/CD tasks such as triggering releases, handling failed deployments, and performing rollbacks
- Provide runbooks or troubleshooting guides for frequent pipeline failures and known issues, with clear steps for diagnosis and resolution
- Document environment topology and promotion flows (e.g., how code moves from dev to QA to staging to production) as driven by pipelines
- Keep records of dependency on external systems (e.g., test data services, external APIs, shared infrastructure) that pipelines rely upon
- Embed inline documentation and comments within pipeline configuration files to explain non-obvious logic, constraints, and workarounds
- Contribute to internal wikis, knowledge bases, or playbooks that formalize CI/CD best practices and organizational standards
- Share knowledge through demos, brown-bag sessions, or internal workshops on CI/CD topics relevant to the team’s stack and practices
- Ensure that documentation is versioned along with pipeline code, and kept aligned with actual implemented behavior during changes
- Advocate for documentation updates as part of change reviews so that pipeline and release processes remain understandable to all stakeholders","is_non_core_section":true}]}
